title: Entomoscope & ENIMAS
summary: From specimens to usable images: I lead AI development and integrate analysis into the Entomoscope imaging workflow.
problem: Digitizing small insects requires controlled imaging and a practical connection between hardware and analysis.
contribution: I lead AI development for the Entomoscope photomicroscope and contribute to its integration with the DiversityScanner robotic ecosystem.
method: ENIMAS connects image acquisition with analysis workflows for species identification, orientation, sex classification, and anatomical segmentation.
evidence: The Entomoscope 2.0 / ENIMAS 2.0 preprint describes the platform. Related specimen-triage research evaluates downstream analysis tasks.

title: InsectMorphoAI
summary: Measurements from images: I develop software to estimate insect length, volume, and biomass for ecological research.
problem: Manual measurements limit the scale of insect trait and biomass studies.
contribution: I develop the image-based software suite and deep learning workflows for insect morphometric analysis.
method: Oriented bounding boxes support rapid measurement; anatomical segmentation supports more detailed, taxon-specific estimates from 2D images.
evidence: Published in Ecological Informatics in 2026, with taxon-specific volumetric validation. Estimates depend on the imaging setup and the taxa evaluated.

title: FORSAID
summary: Vision for forest surveillance: I develop classifiers for regulated forest pests within the FORSAID project.
problem: Recognizing regulated pests in trap images is difficult when species look similar and imaging conditions vary.
contribution: I contribute deep learning classifiers to work package 3: digital technologies for ground detection and surveillance of regulated pests.
method: Image-based species recognition connects computer vision with expert taxonomic knowledge in the Horizon Europe FORSAID project (grant 101134200).
evidence: The Agrilus recognition study investigates neural networks for forest pest surveillance, including evaluation on specimen images.

title: Robotic specimen handling
summary: Connecting specimen handling, imaging, and AI-assisted analysis.
problem: Small, fragile biological specimens are difficult to handle and document consistently.
contribution: I contribute AI analysis and collaborate with engineers and taxonomists to connect robotic imaging with specimen-level information.
method: The broader research spans flexible gripping, close-range imaging, orientation and sex classification, and anatomical segmentation.
evidence: Related publications cover flexible gripping, specimen triage, and acoustic levitation for multi-view imaging.

title: Turbine maintenance optimization
summary: Optimization and data tools for industrial maintenance workflows.
problem: Industrial maintenance planning requires usable decision support and consistent data workflows.
contribution: As a Data Scientist Consultant at Modis / Baker Hughes, I developed a turbine-maintenance optimization algorithm, led cloud data migration, and built workflow automation tools.
method: Optimization, data migration, and Microsoft Power Platform automation supported internal maintenance and information workflows.
evidence: Professional work at Modis / Baker Hughes, February 2022–March 2023. No public implementation or quantified performance results are presented here.

title: Carbon stock estimation from satellite imagery
summary: Semantic segmentation and satellite data analysis for environmental measurement.
problem: Estimating carbon stocks from satellite imagery requires structured geospatial data and image interpretation.
contribution: At Plasive Technologies, I designed and trained CNN segmentation models, developed a carbon stock estimation method, and constructed a multidimensional satellite-image dataset.
method: Semantic segmentation of satellite imagery combined with remote sensing and data analytics.
evidence: Professional work at Plasive Technologies in 2021. No public dataset, implementation, or validated performance figures are claimed here.
